To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mind-set of a person is a function of his or her culture.

(1) The cultural mind-set is a cognitive structure that is activated when a person is engaged in a cultural activity, and it consists of cultural knowledge that is relevant to the activity, (2) cultural mind-sets are situated in the sense that they are activated by cultural activity and are not stable across different activities, (3) cultural mind- sets are activated in different ways by different types of cultural activity (e.g. by reading a book, by talking to a native speaker), and
the mind-set for culture as situated cognition is not a single mind-set, but a collection of mind-sets, each of which has its own unique characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of cultural differences in cognition.
the role of culture in shaping the cognitive processes of the mind.
the development of the concept of culture in relation to situated cognition and the implications for clinical practice and research.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
culture is a situated cognition, which is a social construction that is a part of our mind-sets and that it is the mind-sets of individuals and groups that are the foundation of culture.
the culture of the organization is an important factor for the performance of the employees.
culture is a situated cognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mind-sets of people are not fixed, but can be changed.
culture is situated cognition.
culture is a set of mind-sets that are shared by a group of individuals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
culture is not a fixed, stable entity but rather a dynamic process that is continually being constructed and reconstructed through interaction.
the concept of situated cognition, which emphasizes how knowledge and skills are shaped by context, can help to understand the relationship between culture and cognition.
culture is not an entity that exists in the mind, or in the head, as some sort of mental program.
